utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be seated. Good afternoon to everybody. May we please hear the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Case number IT-94-2-PT, the Prosecutor versus Dragan Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. May I ask you, Mr. Nikolic: Can you follow the proceedings in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. May I then have the appearances, please, for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. YAPA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Appearances for the Prosecution: Myself, Upawansa Yapa; Ms. Patricia Sellers; and Mr. William Smith. Ms. Boles is the case manager. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And for the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's Howard Morrison, lead counsel for the defendant; co-counsel, Tanja Radosavljevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Today we'll conduct a Status Conference, and let me start immediately with the question that we had already last time before us. Did the parties come to any agreement? And if so, could you please be so kind and explain the agreement to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the answer to the question is in the affirmative. There is an agreement, and a copy will, I anticipate, instantly be supplied to you. When that has happened, I would ask that the defendant, Mr. Nikolic, be re-arraigned on the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. May I ask the Prosecution: Could you please explain the main details of the agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. YAPA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. In addition to what my learned friend stated just now, may I say that before Your Honours we have filed a joint motion. The motion has been filed confidentially. And attached to the motion we have an agreement, a plea agreement, also confidentially. And as to the plea agreement, there is the former documents that have been filed in this case, the indictment that was read out to the accused some time back, and the translations of the indictment and the documents. Before I get on to the plea agreement as such, may I mention the reasons for filing the joint motion and the plea agreement confidentially. Actually, it was because of some of the terms in the plea agreement. So in my address before Your Honours now, in respect of the plea agreement, I will refer to the passages in the plea agreement which can be in the open. There will not be any problem in respect of those. But there may be certain areas which will have to be kept confidentially, so those I will not be mentioning. And Your Honour, may I ask the Defence and myself in respect of those paragraphs which I will not be mentioning. Basically, the plea agreement is that the accused has agreed to plead guilty to the indictment in its entirety; that is, the indictment of four charges against him, he has agreed; and also at the same time he agrees with the factual basis, the facts which supported the charges against him. Your Honours will be pleased to see in paragraph 1 of the plea agreement we state that the document constitutes the plea agreement between the accused, Dragan Nikolic, through his counsel, Howard Morrison, and the Office of the Prosecutor. The purpose of this agreement is set forth in its entirety: the understanding of the parties as to the nature of the agreement; the consequences of Dragan Nikolic's plea of guilty; and to assist the Trial Chamber in ensuring, pursuant to Rule 62 bis of the Tribunal's Rules of Procedure and Evidence, that the plea is voluntary and informed; and to set forth the factual basis for the crimes and his participation in those crimes. This is -- of course, we are repeating the Rules applicable, which Your Honours are well aware of. Then in respect to the terms of the agreement, there are certain passages which I'm sure my learned friend will refer to, because it is a joint motion. These are the undertakings of the accused. Paragraph 3 refers to what the accused has -- Dragan Nikolic has undertaken. In respect of the nature of the offence, Your Honours will be pleased to see in III there is the legal basis, and what the accused understands in pleading guilty in respect of the counts that -- the charges, the crimes with which he has been charged. Paragraph 10 of the plea agreement, which is at page 5, is an important one. The factual basis established in the crimes described in count 1 to 4, Dragan Nikolic's part is contained in the third amended indictment which is attached to this agreement. Dragan Nikolic has reviewed with his attorney the factual basis and agrees with the specific factual allegations set forth therein. There is reference to the consideration by the Prosecutor in V. Now, in respect of this, since there is certain section which is VI and since 12(1) has a bearing on that paragraph, that is, paragraph 6, I shall not be making reference to paragraph 1, but if Your Honours please, Your Honours will be pleased to question me on that. But I submit to Your Honours that one is linked to VI. In fact, it is paragraph 13 of the agreement. We have made a request in this plea agreement that the Prosecutor and the Defence, that the Trial Chamber schedule a public sentencing hearing within which both parties may submit any relevant evidence that may assist the Trial Chamber in determining an appropriate sentence, pursuant to Rule 100. Then also it is stated - this is also a consideration by the Prosecutor - that the accused's plea represents a full accounting of his criminal behaviour in April 1992, and including September 1992, whether or not all of the accused's crimes have been included in the third amended indictment. Then also the Prosecutor will advise any national domestic court regarding the accused's culpability for any further crimes alleged from April 1992 until and including September 1992. That they have been dealt with by way of the sentence provided by the Trial Chamber. Of course, this is something to happen in the future. Five, that regarding the accused's criminal conducting in Vlasenica from April 1992 until and including September 1992, that the Tribunal's Office of the Prosecutor has primacy over the Prosecution of those crimes. There is a paragraph in VII that is in respect of the again on the part of the accused, which will be explained by my learned friend. Then we have also, which is for Your Honours' consideration, in paragraph 8, a declaration by the accused. Then the plea agreement ends with the declaration by counsel, and also it is stated except as expressly set forth in this agreement, there are no additional promises, understandings or agreements between the Office of the Prosecutor and Dragan Nikolic or his counsel, Mr. Howard Morrison. That's the explanation that I could provide to you. I thank you Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I ask the Prosecution: Is there any recommendation on the sentence?

utterances.speaker: MR. YAPA
utterances.text: There is. This is the paragraph that I made reference to, that is, the paragraph 1, coming under 12, subparagraph 1 under 12, under V, consideration by the Prosecutor, there is a recommendation that has been made by the Prosecution. Your Honour will be pleased to see that it has to be linked with paragraph 13.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: As for reasons of transparency, may I ask what is the recommendation of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. YAPA
utterances.text: The Prosecution has recommended a 15-year term.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. May I ask the Defence: What about your contribution, waive of rights and so on, before we turn to the accused himself?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Your Honours, of course, those matters set forth by my learned friend for the Prosecution are accurate and indeed a repetition of the matters set out verbatim in the plea agreement. I would specifically draw Your Honours' attention to IV, penalty, paragraph 11. I say at this stage because it's in counterpoint to the matter just raised by my learned friend as to the recommendation. For the sake of transparency, so that all those understand that the powers of the Court are, as I'm about to describe, I read it verbatim: "Dragan Nikolic understands the maximum sentence that could be imposed by the Trial Chamber for a guilty plea to the crimes in the third amended indictment, is a term of imprisonment up to and including the remainder of his life as described in Rule 101 A. In determining the sentence the Trial Chamber shall take into consideration such factors as the gravity of the offence any aggravating or mitigating circumstances, including the substantial cooperation with the Prosecutor by the convicted person before or after the conviction and the individual circumstances of the convicted person pursuant to Article 24(2) of the Statute and Rule 101(b). The Prosecutor and the Defence understand the Trial Chamber is not bound by any agreement of sentence specified by the parties." That, of course, as Your Honours are well aware, is a standard paragraph which would be included in any such plea agreement. My learned friend made a reference to, under V, 12(1), being linked to the matters in the agreement under VI, paragraph 13. It really comes to this: There is part of the agreement which, at the sentencing hearing, will be fully aired and understood by all parties concerned. At the moment, it is not necessary for any of the parties to go into that in any detail, because if it did, it may be that there would be difficulties in the Defence adducing all of the matters that it wished to adduce by way of mitigation in this case, and out of fairness to the accused I know no one would want to put any hampering or break on that. So unless asked to do so, I say no more about that. I go on to the waiver of rights, which is under VII, beginning paragraph 14. I summarise, because it is there set forth verbatim: The defendant understands by virtue of pleading guilty he gives up his right to plead not guilty and to require the Prosecution to prove the charges in the indictment beyond a reasonable doubt. The right to prepare and put forward a defence to the charges as opposed to a mitigation, of course; the right to be tried without undue delay; the right to be tried in his presence and to defend himself in person at trial, the right to examine at his trial or have examined the witnesses against him. I summarise, but basically -- I should add to testify against himself or confess guilt. But the last is, as it were, unimportant, because, of course, that's the purpose of this hearing today. In other words, the accused fully understands that by pleading guilty he does not have the right to the trial process. He has a right to a sentencing process and for mitigation to be placed before the Court before any determination of sentence, and of course by pleading guilty he doesn't waive his right to be represented by counsel at all stages he goes on under VIII paragraph 16, and I will read this verbatim, it's signed by the defendant: "I Dragan Nikolic have read this plea agreement including the attached third amended indictment which sets forth in its entirety the understanding of the parties and having carefully reviewed every part of it with my attorney Howard Morrison" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Counsel please slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: -- "to the elements of the offences charged." I'm sorry. "-- of possible defences and of the consequences of entering into the agreement. No promises or inducements have been made to me other than those contained in this agreement. Furthermore, no one has threatened me or forced me in any way to enter into this agreement, and I have entered into this agreement freely and voluntarily, and I am of sound mind. I understand the terms of this agreement and I voluntarily agree to each of the terms." And it is dated the 2nd of September of 2003 and signed by the defendant, Dragan Nikolic. And under IX, paragraph 17, there is a mirrored declaration of the important matters, and that's also dated the 2nd of September and signed by myself. Your Honour, unless I'm asked to either go into any more detail or make any specific explanation of any other matter, that's the Defence contribution at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you very much. It's my understanding that there are no additional promises or other agreements besides the one cited by you. I see both parties nodding. May I then ask you, Mr. Dragan Nikolic, in person: Have you ever been threatened or forced in any way before entering into this agreement?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Neither any of my attorneys or anybody else, my family members or anybody else, influenced me in coming to this decision. It is my own personal decision, and I have nothing further to add. There were no threats, no suggestions either way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: No promises, no inducements?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely none.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I ask, in addition: Did you understand all the terms of this agreement and was it read to you in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it was read out to me twice. I had two or three meetings with my attorneys and we went through the document point by point. All the points of the agreement were explained to me, and I am fully conscious of what the agreement contains. So that I am fully apprised of it and everything is clear to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: One crucial point is no doubt the one already mentioned beforehand, that according to Rule 62 ter (B), the Trial Chamber -- I quote from our Rules: "The Trial Chamber shall not be bound by any agreement specified in paragraph A." And as it was already verbatim read out by your counsel, it is your understanding that the maximum sentence that could be imposed by the Trial Chamber for a guilty plea to the crimes in the third amended indictment is a term of imprisonment up to and including the remainder of your life, as described in Rule 101(A) of our Rules. Of course, it's today not the time to discuss sentence when we don't have the necessary facts. Of course, we have to take into account and into consideration all the facts, such as the gravity, aggravating, mitigating circumstances, and whether or not you're ready for substantial cooperation with the Prosecutor. But it has to be absolutely clear that a recommendation by the Prosecution is nothing more but a recommendation, and the final arbiter for the sentence is no doubt the Bench, this Trial Chamber. Did you understand this?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, in full.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I then ask you: Are you prepared to change your plea? Until now you had pleaded not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I am prepared, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then let us, for a better understanding, proceed in the following way: I will read out paragraph by paragraph the indictment, and if you could be so kind and answer whether the statement contained in this paragraph is correct or not. I don't want to follow the order of the indictment, because for a better understanding it is easier to start with paragraph 36, the general legal allegations, and then followed by additional facts. It starts with saying: "All acts or omissions charged as crimes against humanity occurred during an armed conflict in Bosnia-Herzegovina and were related to a widespread or systematic attack directed against a civilian population, specifically the Muslim and non-Serb population of the Vlasenica municipality." Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: "The municipality (opstina) of Vlasenica is in eastern Bosnia and Herzegovina, approximately 50 kilometres west of the Serbian border and approximately 120 kilometres north-east of Sarajevo. According to the 1991 census, the municipality had approximately 33.817 citizens, of whom approximately 55 per cent were Muslim, 47 [sic] were Serb, and 2 were described as 'other.' The town of Vlasenica is located within the municipality of the same name. In 1991, the town of Vlasenica had approximately 7.500 citizens, approximately 65 per cent of whom were Muslim and 35 per cent were Serb." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I assume it is. These are data, official data. I have not checked them out, but I do believe that that is so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: You have no reason to doubt these figures; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct. I have no reason to doubt them, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: "In January 1992, Serbs from Vlasenica and eight neighbouring municipalities declared the area to be the 'Birac Autonomous Region' within the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. Tensions increased in the spring of 1992 with the referendum on the proposed independence of Bosnia-Herzegovina." Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: "About 21 April 1992, Serb forces took over the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. town of Vlasenica and declared it to be a Serbian town JNA soldiers, including soldiers purporting to be from the Novi Sad corps from Serbia, paramilitary forces and local military soldiers participated in the takeover. During the day, police vehicles drove around Vlasenica town and issued an ultimatum over loudspeakers for Muslims to turn in their weapons. The Muslim population complied with the ultimatum and did not resist." Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: "Once the Serbs took control of the municipality, the Crisis Staff ( Krizni Stab) administered the town and appointed Serbs to all official positions. Local Serb men were mobilised and took over military responsibilities from the JNA forces. Among other things, local Serb military forces guarded important facilities and later were formed into companies and used to search surrounding woods for armed Muslims."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: "After the takeover, conditions for Muslims and other non-Serbs in the municipality deteriorated. The Serb authorities fired Muslims and other non-Serbs from their jobs and limited their withdrawal of funds from banks. The Serb authorities did not permit the Muslims and other non-Serbs to travel without special passes. Muslim men were frequently arrested and brought to the police station for interrogation. Beatings and murders sometimes accompanied the interrogations." Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: "Many Muslims and other non-Serbs fled the Vlasenica area, and beginning in May 1992 and continuing until September 1992, those Muslims and other non-Serbs who had remained were either forcibly expelled or arrested. By September 1992, virtually no Muslims or other non-Serbs remained in Vlasenica."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: "The Serb forces initially held the arrested Muslims and other non-Serbs either at a local school or the local prison in Vlasenica. In approximately late May or early June 1992, the Serb forces established a detention camp at Susica, the main detention facility in the Vlasenica area, and sent the arrested Muslims and the non-Serbs there. Susica camp was run by the military and the local police militia. The camp guards were generally soldiers from the local area."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: "Susica camp was located approximately one kilometre from the town of Vlasenica, in a military facility that had previously been used for storage of military equipment. Men, women, and children were kept in the camp; however, the women and children generally stayed for only short periods of time before being forcibly transferred to nearby Muslim areas. Before being forcibly transferred, non-Serbs usually had to sign a document stating that they were leaving the area voluntarily and that they were giving up their possessions."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: "Susica camp consisted of two main buildings: A warehouse or hangar ('the hangar'), 50 metres by 30 metres, which was used to house the detainees and a second smaller building which was used for storage of uniforms and equipment. There was also a small house used by the guards and commander of the camp to interrogate detainees when they arrived. Between late May and October 1992, as many as 8.000 Muslim civilians and other non-Serbs from Vlasenica and the surrounding villages were detained in the hangar in Susica camp."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: "The number of detainees in the hangar at any one time varied, but was generally between 300 and 500 detainees. The building was severely overcrowded, detainees were not provided with anything to sleep on, toilet facilities were limited, and there were no showers. The food provided was sparse and often spoiled. The guards brutally beat the detainees on a daily basis. Many detainees died from the beatings by the guards."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: "Many of the detained women were subjected to sexual assaults, including rape. Camp guards or other men who were allowed to enter the camp frequently took women out of the hangar at night. When the women returned, they were often in a traumatised state and other detainees observed that the women were distraught."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: After this general description, let us now turn to the core issue, your individual alleged criminal responsibility. It reads in this third amended indictment: "The Prosecution of this Tribunal against Dragan Nikolic, that the Prosecutor of the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia, pursuant to her authority under Article 18 of the Statute of the Tribunal, charges you, Dragan Nikolic, also known as Jenki, with crimes against humanity, as set forth below: "The accused Dragan Nikolic, born on 26 April 1957, is from the town of Vlasenica in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Before the war, he worked at the Alpro aluminum factory in Vlasenica. He lived with his family on Zarka Vukovica Street in the Krusevik section of Vlasenica. From at least early June 1992 until about 30 September 1992, Dragan Nikolic was a commander of Susica detention camp in Vlasenica." Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then let us turn to paragraph 2, where we have the general allegations under Article 7 of the Statute of the Tribunal. The Trial Chamber has some problems with the mere repetition of Article 7(1) of the Statute. May I ask the Prosecution in this context: Do you want to amend the indictment?

utterances.speaker: MR. YAPA
utterances.text: I'm thankful to Your Honours for raising this matter at this stage. This is a matter that was given consideration, and I have discussed this matter with my learned friend as well. And may I, with Your Honours' permission, move to have the indictment amended by substituting certain words to this paragraph and certain other paragraphs in the indictment? It is not a substantial change as such. It's not in substance, but it is, I should say, more refining the indictment. My application is that paragraph 2 be read as follows: "Dragan Nikolic is individually criminally responsible, pursuant to Article 7(1), for committing the crimes charged in counts 1, 2, and 4, and for aiding and abetting the execution of the crimes charged in count 3 of this indictment." That is the amendment that I move for in respect of paragraph 2. In respect of count 1, where there is the penal paragraph, paragraph 7, may be read: "Persecutions on political, racial, and religious grounds, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(h) and Article 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal." In respect of count 2, in paragraph 19, may be read: "Murder, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(a) and Article 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal." In respect of count 3, may it read, paragraph 35 --

utterances.speaker: MR. YAPA
utterances.text: 22. I'm sorry. "Rape, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(g) and Article 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal." In respect of count 4, that will be paragraph 35: "Torture, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(f) and Article 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal." Those are the amendments that I move for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. May I hear the Defence on this matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: If it please Your Honour, the Defence was of course aware of the intended application to amend the indictment. It's an amendment which simplifies the indictment and makes it clear exactly upon which basis the defendant is entering his pleas of guilty, and for that reason not only do I not oppose the proposed amendment, but I endorse it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. To make it absolutely clear, it is not intended to change any factual or legal basis, just for purposes of clarification, to delete those words which are not needed for the legal assessment of the factual basis presented in this indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: After having conferred, the Bench is accepting and confirming this amended indictment which forms now the basis for the further proceedings. You understood what was discussed, Mr. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then before turning to the counts as such, let me please go to the single incidents mentioned in these charges.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Count 1, persecutions. "From at least early June 1992 until about 30 September 1992, Dragan Nikolic persecuted the Muslim and non-Serb detainees at Susica camp on political, racial, and religious grounds."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: "Dragan Nikolic persecuted Muslim and non-Serb detainees at the Susica camp by subjecting them to murders, rapes, and torture, as charged specifically in the indictment. In addition, Dragan Nikolic persecuted Muslims and non-Serb detainees by participating in sexual violence directed at women at the Susica camp as set forth in paragraphs 20 and 21 of the indictment." We'll come back to this later. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: "As part of the persecutions, Dragan Nikolic detained Muslim and non-Serbs at the Susica camp and assisted in the forcible transfer of those detained at the camp from the Vlasenica municipality. At the end of June 1992, large numbers of the male detainees were transferred from the camp to the larger Batkovic detention camp near Bijeljina in north-eastern Bosnia and Herzegovina. Most of the women and children detainees were transferred either to Kladanj or Cerska in Bosnian Muslim controlled territory."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: "As part of the persecutions, Dragan Nikolic subjected detainees to an atmosphere of terror, created by the murders, beatings, sexual violence and other physical and mental abuse of detainees and to inhumane living conditions by being deprived of adequate food, water, medical care, sleeping, and toilet facilities. As a result, detainees suffered severe psychological and physical trauma. Dragan Nikolic participated in creating and maintaining this atmosphere of terror and the inhumane conditions." "By his participation in the acts or omissions described in paragraphs 3 through 6, Dragan Nikolic is individually criminally responsible for count 1: Persecutions on political, racial, and religious grounds, a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(h) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal." What is your plea to this count 1?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May we please take it for the record that the accused has pleaded guilty related to count 1 of the indictment. Let us now turn to count 2, murder. "One evening about 13 June 1992 and about 24 June 1992, Dragan Nikolic and other guards at Susica camp entered the hangar building and called out Durmo Handzic and Asim Zildzic. After taking them outside the building, Dragan Nikolic and the guards subjected Durmo Handzic and Asim Zildzic to severe physical abuse, including punching, kicking, and beatings with weapons such as lengths of wood lasting for at least 45 minutes, during which time the two men repeatedly begged for the beating to stop."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: "When the beating concluded, both detainees were brought back to the hangar. Asim Zildzic died shortly after returning. The following morning, upon the order of Dragan Nikolic, two detainees buried Asim Zildzic."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: "Later that morning, Dragan Nikolic entered the hangar and approached Durmo Handzic. Although Handzic was in severe agony from being beaten the night before, Dragan Nikolic demanded information regarding Durmo Handzic's son. Durmo Handzic died shortly after this encounter and was buried that day by other detainees."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: "During the night of 23 and 24 June 1992, Dragan Nikolic entered the hangar and ordered Muharem Kolarevic and Dzevad Saric be taken outside. Sometime after that, other guards removed Ismet Musa Zekic also from the hangar. For approximately 30 minutes after the men were taken from the hangar, detainees inside heard cries of pain and then gunshots that came from a location close to the hangar."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: "After the gunshots were heard, a guard called two detainees from the hangar and ordered them to dispose of the bodies of Muharem Kolarevic and Dzevad Saric behind the hangar. Dragan Nikolic ordered the two detainees to wash away the blood on the ground where the deceased had been beaten."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: "After attempting to wash away the blood, the two detainees waited outside the hangar. As Dragan Nikolic sat inside the nearby guardhouse, the two men watched the same guard who called them out of the hangar shoot and kill Ismet Zekic."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: "Shortly after Ismet Zekic was killed, Dragan Nikolic and the guard who had shot Zekic entered the hangar with some local police. The police pointed at Rasim Ferhatbegovic and asked if he was the one who was running away. The guard who had shot Ismet Zekic said 'yes.' Rasim Ferhatbegovic was then taken outside, and shortly thereafter the other prisoners heard one shot."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: "Early the next morning, Dragan Nikolic entered the hangar and again called out the two detainees who had disposed of the bodies the day before. They went to the area of the camp that was being used as a toilet and found the body of Muharem Kolarevic slumped over a fence, caught in wire. The guard who had shot Ismet Zekic the day before then shot Kolarevic again. The two prisoners then took the body of Muharem Kolarevic to where they had left the bodies the previous evening and there they saw the body of Rasim Ferhatbegovic with a bullet hole in the centre of his forehead."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: "On or about 6 July 1992, Dragan Nikolic took Ismet Dedic out of the hangar at Susica camp and closed the door behind them. Detainees inside the hall then heard Ismet Dedic scream. A few minutes later, Dragan Nikolic directed two detainees to drag Ismet Dedic inside the hangar, where the other detainees could see that Ismet Dedic's body was covered in blood. His body was barely recognisable and he appeared to have suffered serious injuries. Ismet Dedic died shortly thereafter. His body was placed in a plastic bag and removed by other detainees."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: "Mevludin Hatunic, his wife and daughter were detained in Susica camp in early July 1992. Between about 3 July and 7 July 1992, while detained in the camp, Mevludin Hatunic offered his house to a Serb in exchange for moving his family out of the area. Hatunic was then permitted to leave the camp to arrange the transfer of the house. Upon his return, Dragan Nikolic accused Hatunic of having told the Serb to whom he had given his house that Hatunic would 'wait for his opportunity to get even.' That evening, because he had allegedly made such a statement, Dragan Nikolic beat Mevludin Hatunic. The next morning, Dragan Nikolic beat Mevludin Hatunic again, until Mevludin Hatunic lost consciousness. Later that evening, Dragan Nikolic returned and, finding that Mevludin Hatunic had regained consciousness, beat him a third time. A short time later Mevludin Hatunic died as a result of the beatings. His body was placed in a plastic bag and was removed from the hangar by other detainees."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: "From about the second week of July 1992, over a seven-day period, Dragan Nikolic beat Galib Music, a 60-year-old detainee by, among other things, kicking him and beating him with a metal pipe. During the beatings, Dragan Nikolic accused Galib Music of asking a Muslim organisation to come to expel the Serbs from Vlasenica. Each time Dragan Nikolic beat Galib Music, Music lost consciousness, and, after approximately seven days, Galib Music died."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: "By his participation in the acts and omissions described in paragraphs 8 through 18, in relation to Durmo Handzic, Asim Zildzic, Rasim Ferhatbegovic, Muharem Kolarevic, Dzevad Saric, Ismet Zekic, Ismet Dedic, Mevludin Hatunic, and Galib Music, Dragan Nikolic is individually criminally responsible for: Count 2, murder, a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(a) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal." Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. What is your plea?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: For the record, the accused has pleaded guilty in relation to count 2 and all the details, factual details, underlying this count. Count 3, sexual violence: "From early June until about 15 September 1992, many female detainees at Susica camp were subjected to sexual assaults, including rapes and degrading physical and verbal abuse. Dragan Nikolic personally removed and otherwise facilitated the removal of female detainees from the hangar, which he knew was for purposes of rapes and other sexually abusive conduct. The sexual assaults were committed by camp guards, special forces, local soldiers, and other men."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: "Female detainees were sexually assaulted at various locations, such as the guardhouse, the houses surrounding the camp, at the Panorama Hotel, a military headquarters, and at locations where such women were taken to perform forced labour. Dragan Nikolic allowed female detainees, including girls and elderly women, to be verbally subjected to humiliating sexual threats in the presence of other detainees in the hangar. Dragan Nikolic facilitated the removal of female detainees by allowing guards, soldiers, and other males to have access to these women on a repetitive basis and by otherwise encouraging the sexually abusive conduct."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: "By his aiding and abetting in the conduct described in paragraphs 20 and 21, in relation to female detainees in Susica camp, Dragan Nikolic is individually criminally responsible for: Count 3: Rape, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(g), 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I plead guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: For the record, the accused has also pleaded guilty in relation to count 3. Count 4, torture. I apologise if I'm mispronouncing the one or other name. I'm not acquainted with and my sincere apologies if I should do so, especially to relatives of victims. "Fikret 'Cice' Arnaut, from about 1 June to about 18 July 1992, Dragan Nikolic beat Fikret Arnaut by kicking him, stomping on him, and punching him with metal knuckles on his fists. The beatings took place both inside and outside the hangar. Several of the beatings took place in a corner of the hangar known as the 'punishment' corner."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: "On one occasion, Dragan Nikolic came into the hangar and told Fikret Arnaut to kneel on the floor, put his hands behind his head, and tilt his head back. Dragan Nikolic then put a bayonet in his mouth and asked him about his brother, who Dragan Nikolic claimed had joined a group of Ustasha. Later that same day, two men came to the hangar and took Fikret Arnaut outside. When Fikret Arnaut returned, he had been beaten severely and was bleeding from his mouth. Shortly thereafter, Dragan Nikolic came to Fikret Arnaut in the hangar and said words to the effect: 'What? They did not beat you enough. If it had been me, you would not be able to walk. They are not as well trained to beat people as I am.'" Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: "On one occasion, Dragan Nikolic took Fikret Arnaut outside the hangar and beat Fikret Arnaut with metal knuckles. Fikret Arnaut fell to the ground and Dragan Nikolic kicked his ribs and back around the kidney area. During this beating, Dragan Nikolic accused Fikret Arnaut of organising the Muslims."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: "On a subsequent occasion, Dragan Nikolic approached Fikret Arnaut in the hangar and said words to the effect: 'I can't believe how an animal like this can't die. He must have two hearts.' Dragan Nikolic then beat Fikret Arnaut again and stomped on his chest."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: "On 11 June 1992, Sead Ambeskovic was arrested in Vlasenica. Police first interrogated him and then took him to Susica camp. Once in the camp, Dragan Nikolic and others beat Sead Ambeskovic, using axe handles, iron bars, and rifle butts."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: "In the morning of 14 June 1992, guards took Sead Ambeskovic and Hajrudin Osmanovic from the hangar. The two men were ordered to kneel with their hands behind their heads. Dragan Nikolic asked them where their weapons were and to identify others who had weapons. During the interrogation, Dragan Nikolic and others then beat them with iron bars, wooden bats and rifle butts for approximately one and one-half hours. As a result of this beating, the back of Sead Ambeskovic's head was cut, four teeth on the left side of his mouth were knocked out, and three ribs were broken."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: "On or about 16 June 1992, Dragan Nikolic again called Sead Ambeskovic and Hajrudin Osmanovic out of the hangar. Once outside, Dragan Nikolic demanded to know if they had weapons and who else had weapons. Dragan Nikolic and two other guards immediately began beating them with bats for 10 to 15 minutes."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: "On 3 July 1992, Hajrudin Osmanovic was taken from Susica camp to perform forced labour. He has never been seen since."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: "From about 13 June to about 3 July 1992, Suad Mahmutovic suffered frequent, sometimes daily beatings by Dragan Nikolic at Susica camp. Dragan Nikolic beat Suad Mahmutovic with iron bars, rifle butts, and rubber tubing with lead inside. During one beating, several of Suad Mahmutovic's ribs were broken. On separate occasion, Dragan Nikolic kicked Suad Mahmutovic in the face with his boot, which caused a cut that left permanent scars."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: "On one occasion, Dragan Nikolic placed cocked pistol inside Suad Mahmutovic's mouth. Dragan Nikolic tried to force Suad Mahmutovic to admit that his neighbour had a weapon, but Suad Mahmutovic refused. Dragan Nikolic then pulled the trigger but the gun was not loaded."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: "Redzo Caksic was arrested on 2 June 1992 and taken to Susica camp. Upon arrival, Dragan Nikolic and other guards searched him. He was then taken to the hangar, where, with other detainees, he was ordered to line up and lean against the wall with his hands behind his back. Dragan Nikolic then hit Redzo Cakisic, and other detainees, with his rifle butt and kicked them with his boots."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: "Approximately ten days later, Dragan Nikolic called Redzo Cakisic from the hangar during the night. Two men were waiting outside with Dragan Nikolic. Nikolic said to them words to the effect: 'Here, I brought you something for dinner.' The two men who were not camp guards hit Redzo Cakisic in the back with rifle butts and kicked him in the stomach and sides. During this beating, Dragan Nikolic was approximately five metres away in the guardhouse. The beating continued for about 20 minutes."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: "By his participation in the acts and omissions described in the paragraphs 23 through 34, in relation to Fikret 'Cice' Arnaut, Sead Ambeskovic, Hajrudin Osmanovic, Suad Mahmutovic, and Redzo Cakisic, Dragan Nikolic is individually criminally responsible for count 4, torture, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(f), 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: You may be seated. Madam Registrar, may we take to the record that the accused pleaded guilty to all the counts included in the amended indictment. As a consequence of this, this Trial Chamber finds the accused, Dragan Nikolic, guilty of the offences contained in counts 1 through 4 of the indictment just read out before. May I ask the parties: Is it correct that you want to replace the attachment A of your agreement against the newly amended indictment?

utterances.speaker: MR. YAPA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. In due course we'll be filing an amended indictment. For the purpose of the record, it will be filed by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And this would then form attachment A to the plea agreement?

utterances.speaker: MR. YAPA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I hear the Defence on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Your Honour, in the light of that undertaking, I have no observations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: You would accept that this replacement takes place. The question is now the sentencing. Of course, the sentencing has to be well prepared. I took it that the parties would need approximately two months for -- in preparation of the sentencing hearing. Can the parties agree that we already today fix the scheduling for this sentencing hearing for the week -- for the first week of November, that is, 3 through 7 November, knowing that in all likelihood we will not need all the days, but in order to be on the safe side, we should schedule these days. Would these days be suitable for you?

utterances.speaker: MR. YAPA
utterances.text: I'm in agreement, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May we then ask the parties to prepare their respective sentencing briefs no later than Monday, 20 October 2003. Is this convenient? I can see nodding from both sides. May we then turn to another purpose of the Status Conference and ask you, Mr. Nikolic: Do you have any complaints about the situation in the Detention Unit? Do you have any health problems you would draw our attention to?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have no complaints. The conditions are normal, as they have been so far. I have no health problems. As to the rest, I have no complaints with respect to my living in the Detention Unit, as far as the food is concerned, the medical treatment, and all the rest of it. As far as I'm concerned is everything is satisfactory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. May I ask the parties: Are there any other issues to be addressed today? Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. YAPA
utterances.text: We do not have any issues at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. The Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Your Honour, nor I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. The trial then stays adjourned until the 3rd of November, 9.00.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
